newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Fairform seen to issue HK$57 mln shrs in IPO.
newsitem.headline: HK's Fairform seen to issue HK$57 mln shrs in IPO.

text.p: Hong Kong-based household and bathroom products maker Fairform Holdings Ltd is expected to issue 57 million new shares at HK$1.00 each in an initial public offer (IPO) to raise fund for expansion, analysts said.

The issue price will give a prospective price to earnings (P/E) multiple of 6.83 times on a fully-diluted basis and 6.3 times on a weighted average basis, analysts said after attended a company presentation on Friday.
The IPO is expected to run from June 13 to 18 and dealing in the shares is expected to begin by the end of June, they said.
Lippo Securities is seen to be the sponsor of the issue.
Fairform is involved in the design, development, manufacture and sale of over 300 different electric personal care products, electric healthcare products and bathroom products.
It also makes and sells metal parts and plastic tooling, and provision of casing metallisation services.

"The company is expected to use the net proceeds of about HK$50 million for construction of production facilities in China's Dongguan, to develop new products and for working capital," one analyst said.
"It forecast an EPS (earnings per share) of HK$0.1882 for the year ending in December 1997," another analyst said.
Fairform posted profit of HK$27.2 million for the year ended in December 1996, up from HK$24.3 million in 1995 and HK$19 million in 1994.
Turnover rose to HK$310.2 million in 1996, from HK$218.7 million in 1995 and HK$141.9 million in 1994, analysts said.
About 53.7 percent of the company's customers are from Europe, 23.6 percent from North America and 16.1 percent from Asia, they said.
